text: Blessed by Tzeentch, the Earthfire Archers can glimpse the near future. Because the future they perceive is close at hand, they are not bound to silence like the Skyfire Archers, unable to speak of what they foresee. They often inform their enemies of the grim fates awaiting them, sowing terror in their hearts before the battle even begins.
Earthfire Archers can imbue their attacks with magic, striking down even the most heavily armoured foes.
The Tzaangors are an elite breed blessed by Tzeentch, able to peer into futures too deep to fathom. Yet they feel compelled not to speak of what they foresee, leaving their ranks eerily silent.
Skyfire Archers rarely utter a word; all one hears from them is the twang of drawn bowstrings.
The Tzaangors are an elite breed blessed by Tzeentch, able to uncover the secrets hidden within their enemies and chatter them abroad, spreading dread among all who hear.
The Enlightened Ones are simple creatures of mischief, unsettling their enemies' minds even as they cleave their skulls with their weapons.
A flying chariot crewed by devotees of Tzeentch and Tzaangors, striking foes from afar with sorcery while the Tzaangors loose arrows at close range to finish off any who draw near.
Devotees of Tzeentch lead the Tzaangors in ceaseless efforts to disrupt the enemy's battle lines.
Myriad Changes of the Thousand Sons

Legend holds that Tzeentch selected a thousand of the most knowledge-hungry humans from among the Chaos hordes to form this warband, each of them driven by an insatiable thirst for every manner of knowledge.
The Myriad Changes of the Thousand Sons are Tzeentch's most powerful legion in the mortal realm, ever maintained at exactly one thousand strong.

Beastmen are creatures of pure Chaos, and so they serve all four Ruinous Powers equally. Yet sometimes a dam will birth young clearly favoured by the Lord of Change, their hide marked with Tzeentch's brand, or their horns curling into the sign of his foul sigil. These Centigors are as savage and vicious as their non-Tzeentchian kin, but harbour a fiercer resentment for their own clumsy, dim-witted nature, breeding a deep jealousy toward creatures whose minds match their bodies. This jealousy fuels their rage, making them all the more dangerous—and given that Tzeentch himself has touched them, this may be no coincidence at all.
Betrayal, agony, violence, madness... you will taste them all, torn apart by a raging beast...
